content.summary: Reviewed B5 local integration prepares immutable source/registry snapshots and draft Java-host packages, executes real bounded monitoring processes and retains changed/unchanged controls. A three-process Java update preflight passed. Institution-owned host, scheduler, identities and fact/release mappings remain external prerequisites; this phase does not deploy into the bank.
findings: Focused operational tests pass registry tampering, resource-root violations, unsupported config commands, actual two-tick monitor execution, separate Java-host invocation and corrupt JAR refusal.
Timed-out dispatch cleanup freezes and terminates only the dispatch descendants, including workers that create their own process sessions. PID start times guard against reuse.
Source update preflight changes the expected synthetic gift result TRUE to FALSE with old packages preserved; unrelated control remains unchanged. Overdue and exhausted retries remain explicit.
Authority dependency fingerprints now include identity, aliases and their date/identity evidence editions, preventing stale reuse after metadata or evidence changes.

The full test suite and actual Java source-update acceptance are required for final local acceptance. Global allowance remains 78/100; B4 empirical and B5 operational statuses must remain unfinished in the master state.
